A couple of months in, as the pandemic shifted work to remote, the client reported rising defects, even though the dashboards showed near-complete test coverage. The credibility hit landed in front of both the client and **Accenture** account leadership, who were already accustomed to waterfall delivery.

Matt found that an engineer was building from his own interpretation rather than the backlog story, then writing tests after the code. Coverage looked complete, but defects went undetected. The backlog also contributed: stories lacked defined scenarios and a definition of done, leaving no clear way to test them.

Matt took ownership of the failure rather than defending the metrics. He ran a bottom-up audit of the codebase and test suite, showed the gaps openly, and rebuilt the backlog with SMART, testable stories. He brought frontend and backend TDD experts from Columbus to work alongside the team and redo the code and test cases. Coaching included boot camps, coding katas, practice learning sessions, and pairing through an “I do, we do, you do” progression.

He did not audit who could trigger downstream jobs or email processes, verify that production customer names and email addresses had been scrubbed, or implement compensating controls such as data masking and email interception.
